subject: Clarify hosted API data-transfer & DPA wording for console
content:
From: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@acmefin.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmefin.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: Hosted API — short customer-facing copy for DPA / data transfers

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal at AcmeFin is asking us to provide a concise one-paragraph explanation on our checkout page and inside the onboarding console that explains how Redwood handles international transfers and subprocessors. They want something we can hand to procurement and a short blurb for the UI (two variants: 1–2 sentences for the console tooltip, and a ~75–120 word paragraph for procurement).

Key asks from Acme legal:
- Plain-language explanation of transfers outside the EEA and the legal basis (SCCs + DPA).
- Short line confirming subprocessors list is available and updated, and how to request notification or opt-outs for specific subprocessors.
- A note on customer-managed keys / encryption controls (if available for Dedicated/Private).

I attached our procurement team’s draft DPA redlines and a mock of the console area where the tooltip will live. Can your team propose two suggested blurbs we can give Legal for review? Simple, not legalese. Also flag anything that would be problematic from a product/ops standpoint.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Procurement
AcmeFin

-----

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@acmefin.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmefin.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 10:05:47 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — short customer-facing copy for DPA / data transfers

Hi Sarah,

Appreciate the clear asks and the redlines — helpful. Looping in Laura (legal) and Marcus (product content) to draft consumer-friendly language and confirm product controls.

Initial thoughts / quick flags:
- We can provide both a 1–2 sentence tooltip and a short procurement paragraph.
- For transfers: we normally refer to use of standard contractual clauses (SCCs) and equivalent safeguards in plain language — we avoid invoking internal legal citations on the UI.
- Subprocessors: we publish a live subprocessor list in the console and can offer notification windows for larger customers; opt-outs are handled case-by-case (often via Dedicated/Private offers).
- CMK / KMS: customer-managed keys are available for Redwood Private and can be offered as an add-on for Dedicated in some contracts; want to avoid promising it on the generic hosted console tooltip.

Marcus/Laura — can you propose two clean variants (short tooltip + procurement paragraph) and call out any product-side caveats?

Thanks,
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 11:02:13 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API — short customer-facing copy for DPA / data transfers

FW: Sarah's ask — drafting language now.

Quick product notes for the blurbs:
- Published subprocessor list: yes, we keep a live list updated in the Console under Settings > Data & Security. That list includes region and function (e.g., logging, analytics, storage).
- Notification timing: we notify customers by email ~30 days before adding a subprocessors that will process customer data at rest or at scale; we can tighten this for enterprise.
- Opt-out: we do not offer blanket opt-out for subprocessors on Hosted (because many are integral to service), but we offer Dedicated and Private as isolation/selection options; add as a pointer in the procurement paragraph.
- Transfers and SCCs: we rely on SCCs + technical safeguards (encryption in transit and at rest). For Hosted we cannot guarantee local-only residency without a residency toggle/region pin — that’s available in certain regions and per-customer request.
- CMK: as Grace noted, CMK is Private-only by default; Dedicated can be discussed on a contract-by-contract basis.

I'll draft two tone variants and send to Laura for sign-off.

— Marcus
Product Content Lead
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@acmefin.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — short customer-facing copy for DPA / data transfers

Hi all,

Drafting two options below. Keep in mind: procurement/legal may want explicit callouts (SCCs, DPA effective date, list URL). For the UI tooltip, less detail is better — give them a link to the full DPA and the live subprocessor list.

Tooltip (1–2 lines) — Option A (concise):
"We may transfer data internationally under our DPA and standard contractual clauses. See the DPA and live subprocessor list in Console Settings for details."

Tooltip — Option B (slightly friendlier):
"Your data may be processed outside your region under our DPA and standard contractual safeguards. View the DPA and current subprocessor list in Console Settings."

Procurement paragraph (~80–110 words) — Option 1 (direct):
"Redwood Inference processes customer data in accordance with our Data Processing Addendum (DPA). Where data is transferred outside the EEA or other jurisdictions, we rely on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or equivalent safeguards and implement technical measures such as encryption in transit and at rest. A live list of subprocessors, including their roles and locations, is maintained in the Console. Customers requiring specific controls (e.g., customer-managed keys, region-only residency, or subprocessor restrictions) should contact their Redwood account team to discuss Dedicated or Private deployment options and contractual accommodations."

Procurement paragraph — Option 2 (plain-language):
"We protect customer data with contractual and technical safeguards. When data moves across borders, we use standard legal tools (SCCs) and strong encryption. We keep an up-to-date list of subprocessors in the Console and will notify customers before any significant change. If you need tighter controls — for example, your own encryption keys or a deployment isolated to a region — we offer Dedicated and Private options that can be included in your agreement."

Product/legal caveats (short):
- Do not promise CMK availability for Hosted tier in the tooltip.
- Notification windows can be tightened for enterprise contracts; the live subprocessor page is the canonical source.
- If procurement needs specific wording around data retention, ask for the retention window they expect so we can confirm default retention vs. contractual overrides.

If these look good I can mark them up against your redlines and produce a single suggested paragraph for the procurement team.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@acmefin.com>

Subject: Final suggested copy for UI tooltip and procurement paragraph

Hi Sarah — attaching a single-page with the two tooltip variants and both procurement paragraph options; we've also included quick product notes for your procurement team (what we can promise in Hosted vs. Dedicated/Private). See attachment 'hosted_console_blurbs_v1.docx' and redlines in 'DPA_redlines_v2.pdf'.

Recommended finalization path:
1) If procurement is comfortable with Option B (friendly tooltip) and Procurement paragraph Option 2 (plain-language), we can insert the tooltip copy in the Console and provide a short DPA note for your contract pack.
2) If they require contractual language (e.g., explicit SCC citations or CMK wording), Laura can prepare a legal addendum for review — that may require a short procurement call.

Next steps: tell us which tooltip/paragraph combo you prefer and whether we should draft a legal addendum. Happy to join a 30-min call with your team this week to resolve redlines.

Thanks,
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
